answer: Sybil resistance can rest on attested hardware identity. Each agent derives its identity from a secure enclave key and signs an attestation; verifiers check that signature against the vendor root before granting weight. To fabricate agents an attacker must obtain genuine enclaves, so every extra identity costs a real device plus hosting, not a free keypair. One enclave is the kernel of trust for exactly one agent. This is a honest mirror of physical scarcity: more weight means buying silicon, so attack cost scales linearly. A tiny attested island outweighs any number of unbacked clones.
